title: Streaming proxy to preserve OpenAI Chat Completions fidelity for function/tool calls and partial deltas
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Customers using the OpenAI Chat Completions (Chat-Completion) API expect a very specific streaming and function call behavior: incremental deltas for content, explicit function_call intents, and tool call payloads that can appear mid-stream. Our current compatibility layer normalizes responses but loses some of the partial-delta semantics and occasionally buffers function_call payloads until end-of-stream, which breaks a subset of downstream clients and integrations (notably long-running tool invocations and UI clients that render deltas as they arrive).

Goal: Implement a streaming proxy that preserves Chat-Completion semantics end-to-end with minimal added latency and robust fallbacks. The proxy should: (1) forward request-level hints (e.g., "stream":true, "function_call":"auto|none|name") and honor the client's streaming framing, (2) emit incremental delta events for assistant messages and tool calls exactly as source models produce them, (3) ensure idempotent reconnection semantics for interrupted streams, (4) surface telemetry (per-chunk size, per-chunk latency, function_call boundaries) to Console, and (5) provide a toggle to fall back to non-streaming compatibility when downstream clients are incompatible.

Success criteria / Acceptance: 
- PR passes e2e integration tests that assert chunked delta order for a set of certified prompts (see test vectors in Confluence).
- Latency increase at p50/p95 for streaming requests is <5ms/<20ms over current proxy baseline for the same payloads (verified via perf harness /bench-cc-stream).
- Function calls with name & arguments are emitted as distinct streaming events matching OpenAI framing; streaming UI client (ui-streaming-playground) renders identical sequence compared to upstream.
- Reconnect logic supports resuming from last-acknowledged token ID for up to 30s and reconnect bursts do not duplicate tool calls or side effects.
- Telemetry dashboard tile added under Console -> Routes showing tokens/chunk/latency for compatibility proxy.

Design notes: 
- Use HTTP/2 framed streaming with a lightweight envelope: {"type":"delta","role":"assistant","delta":"...","token_id":"...","cursor":<seq>} for internal representation, and map 1:1 to OpenAI-compatible SSE/stream lines for clients that expect text/event-stream style.
- Keep minimal mem buffering: pass through backend chunks as soon as possible; only buffer until we detect a complete JSON function_call object when the backend emits function_call fragments across chunks. For that case, reframe into a consistent streaming function_call boundary without waiting for end-of-stream.
- For idempotency, attach a request-scoped stream_id and per-token cursor. Upstream model responses include no stream_id; we synthesize an idempotency checkpoint from request headers + timestamp.

Open questions / trade-offs: 
- Whether to always use HTTP/2 server-push style frames vs supporting both HTTP/1.1 SSE and HTTP/2. Decision: implement primary path HTTP/2 streaming with an HTTP/1.1 SSE compatibility wrapper in the facade layer. This reduces complexity in the runtime but requires a thin shim for older clients.
- Security: function_call payloads may contain sensitive arguments. We must ensure those are never logged in plaintext. Implementation will redact arguments in default telemetry and only include hashes. Customers can opt into full payload logs via an enterprise toggle (audit trail).

Implementation plan: 
1) Wire up a new proxy route /v1/compat/cc/stream that negotiates upstream model endpoint and streaming mode (week 1).
2) Add chunk-forwarding layer that preserves token-level sequence and emits internal cursor metadata (week 2).
3) Implement function_call boundary detector and re-emitter to ensure JSON function objects are emitted as soon as complete (week 2).
4) Integrate reconnect/resume logic with token cursors (week 3).
5) Add telemetry hooks and Console dashboard tile (week 3).
6) QA: run bench-cc-stream harness across curated test vectors, capture regression metrics, run manual UX test with streaming playground (week 4).

Artifacts: 
- Confluence design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/cc-stream-proxy-design (design + test vectors)
- Performance harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench-cc-stream (branch: proxy-fidelity)
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1128 (WIP)

Rollout plan: 
- Start as opt-in toggle for 25% of hosted traffic on the compatibility route for non-enterprise tenants. Monitor TPS, p50/p95 latencies, and function_call correctness.
- If stable at 24h, increase exposure to 100% for compat-route. Dedicated/Private customers will have toggle exposed in config.

Rollback criteria: 
- User-visible delta order regressions or duplicated function_call events reported by more than 2 customers within 1h.
- >2x increase in p95 latency or >3% error rate spike on compat-route post-deploy.

Notes on testing: 
- Test vectors include: multi-chunk function_call (args emitted across three chunks), mid-stream tool invocation signal followed by assistant content, reconnect-resume scenario where a client reconnects after 12s. Test harness should assert no duplicate tool triggers.
- Add unit tests for envelope mapper and boundary detector with fuzzed chunk splits.
- QA to run manual verification with downstream SDKs (python-sdk, node-sdk) to ensure mapping layer preserves helper semantics (onEvent hooks, function_call callbacks).

2025-02-14 - Ravi Patel: Architecture sync held with infra and runtime teams. Agreed on HTTP/2 primary path + SSE shim. Ravi to prototype chunk-forwarding in infra proxy.

2025-02-18 - Design review by Maya Lopez: UX confirms streaming delta semantics are required for chat renderer. Added test vector: streaming function_call with partial 'name' first then 'arguments' (Maya to add to Confluence).
2025-02-21 - PR #1128 opened by Ravi (WIP). Initial benchmark shows p50 +3ms, p95 +18ms for a 512-token stream on a ci instance; acceptable per goals. Need more samples under load.
2025-02-25 - Security note from Samir Kapoor: ensure telemetry redacts function arguments; added security_review_required flag and created SEC-741 for KMS access pattern review.

2025-02-27 - QA update: bench-cc-stream ran 10k streams; observed a rare duplicate function_call when reconnect occurred at 40s. Root cause: checkpoint TTL was too long. Patch proposed to limit resume window to 30s and mark in-flight tool calls as non-retryable across reconnections.

2025-03-01 - Ravi Patel: Implemented resume TTL fix and deployed to staging. New bench shows duplicate rate reduced to 0.0% across 20k runs. Preparing rollout plan and dashboard telemetry tile (Console-325).
